description: Hi, I’m Rafiull Bari from Bangladesh. I love space and have experience with Python simulations, 3D design, and satellite data. Our team, Astro Kitty, is building a browser game where kids train as astronauts and protect a Mars base from solar storms inspired by real NASA data. Join us to make space science fun for young learners! We welcome teammates interested in web development, game design, animation, or science communication. Beginners are welcome.
summary:
Astro Kitty Mission Trainer is a browser game that puts kids ages 7–12 in charge of a Mars mission. Players train on Earth, travel to Mars, explore its surface in 3D, and build an outpost. With help from Dhrubo, their robot guide, they learn to balance power, food, water, and crew safety. When a solar storm approaches, they face a choice: how much water can they use for radiation shielding while keeping enough for the crew and greenhouse?

The game uses real NASA solar flare records to inspire simulated challenges and labels which information comes from NASA. By seeing the consequences of their choices and trying again, young players discover why astronauts and engineers have to make trade-offs to keep a mission running.
details:
🐱🚀 Astro Kitty Mission Trainer

Train on Earth. Journey to Mars. Build a home among the stars.

An interactive browser game for children aged 7–12, created for the NASA Space Apps Challenge 2026 and the challenge “Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer.”

🎮 Play the Game · 💻 Explore the Source Code

🌟 About the Project

Astro Kitty turns space exploration challenges into hands-on adventures. Players become kitten astronauts and learn by experimenting, making decisions, and watching their choices shape a mission.

With Dhrubo (ধ্রুব), their friendly robot companion, players train on Earth, plan a flight to Mars, explore a walkable 3D world, and manage an outpost. Each activity connects a playful task to a scientific idea or engineering problem.

🌍 Train at Earth Academy

The journey begins at a fictional space training centre in Khulna, Bangladesh. Five practical learning areas introduce essential concepts:

Buoyancy: Balancing forces and practising steady movement.

Rover navigation: Planning routes and testing commands.

Growing food: Managing the conditions plants need.

Gravity: Comparing how objects fall.

Life support: Understanding air, water, and essential systems.

Short instructions, visual feedback, and opportunities to retry encourage children to learn at their own pace.

🚀 Plan a Journey to Mars

Players choose their launch timing, propulsion, trajectory, and landing equipment, then watch their plan unfold.

Animated outcomes reveal how each choice affects the journey, helping players identify problems and improve their next attempt.

🪐 Explore Mars in 3D

A walkable Mars environment features 24 missions across six chapters. Players can:

  • Clean dust from solar panels.
  • Collect rock samples and operate scientific tools.
  • Drive a rover across the terrain.
  • Repair equipment and restore essential systems.
  • Produce oxygen and care for a space garden.

The landscape is an illustrative game environment, designed to make exploration accessible and engaging.

🏠 Keep an Outpost Running

The outpost simulation challenges players to manage a base for five Martian days, balancing power, water, food, and crew safety.

Resources serve competing needs. Water allocated to radiation shielding, for example, must be balanced against the needs of the crew and greenhouse. Players discover how one decision can affect several connected systems.

🛠️ Built With

  • HTML and CSS — page structure, responsive layouts, and styling.
  • JavaScript and TypeScript — gameplay, simulations, and interactions.
  • Three.js — the interactive 3D environment.
  • Canvas and SVG — illustrated scenes and animated elements.
  • Browser audio and narration — guidance and sound feedback.
  • Service workers and local storage — offline support after initial loading and saved progress.

♿ Designed for Young Explorers

The experience includes keyboard and touch controls, captions, reduced-motion support, short instructions, and opportunities to retry without punishment. Mobile performance and readability shaped the design throughout development.

Bengali names and words of encouragement bring our team’s cultural identity into the adventure.

🤖 SI-Assisted Development

ChatGPT/Codex and Claude assisted with coding, debugging, gameplay development, and educational text. ElevenLabs was used to generate Dhrubo’s narration. Our team directed the concept, selected scientific resources, and reviewed and refined the resulting content.

NASA observations are sourced data; gameplay outcomes and visual effects are simplified simulations.

🎯 Our Goal

We want children to understand how a mission’s systems depend on one another—and feel confident experimenting, learning from mistakes, and testing a better solution.
